newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk on trial for Iran dissident killing.
newsitem.headline: Turk on trial for Iran dissident killing.

text.p: An alleged Turkish Islamist hitman went on trial on Monday for the killing of an Iranian dissident and leading Turkish secularists, Anatolian news agency said.
The agency said defendant Irfan Cagirici denied killing dissident Ali Akbar Ghorbani four years ago and Turkish writers Cetin Emec and Turan Dursun in 1990.
"I don't accept any of the accusations," Anatolian quoted him as saying in an Istanbul state security court. A formal plea is not needed under Turkish law.
Turkish media reports alleging that Cagirici had been trained by Iran to kill the country's opponents in Turkey caused a diplomatic row earier this year.
Ghorbani, a member of the Mujahideen Khalq armed opposition group was found dead along with Iranian Abbas Qolizadeh, a supporter of the late Shah, after the two were abducted in Istanbul in 1992.
Anatolian did not say how long a prison sentence Cagirici faced. Turkish television said the trial was adjourned but did not give a resumption date.
